subtopics.title: The Money in Your Hand: What is Interest?

questions.question: What happens to the purchasing power of your money if you leave it hidden under a mattress for 3 years instead of investing it?
options: It buys less because things get more expensive over time.
It buys more because the money ages like fine wine.
It stays exactly the same, so there is no difference.
It earns a small amount of hidden interest.

questions.question: When you put money into an investment account, what is simple interest?
options: Money the bank pays you for using your cash.
Money you pay the bank to keep your cash safe.
A tax the government takes from your savings.
A discount you get on your bank fees.

questions.question: If you invest R2 000, how is the simple interest calculated each year?
options: It is calculated only on the original R2 000 every single year.
It is calculated on the R2 000 plus any interest you already earned.
It goes down every year because you have less time left.
It goes up depending on how much you spend.

subtopics.title: The Final Count: Total Investment Value

questions.question: If you invest R3 000 and earn R450 in simple interest over the period, what is the total value of your investment?
Calculate the total value of an investment if R10 000 is invested at 6% simple interest per annum for 5 years.
Why do we add the interest back to the principal to find the total value?
options: Because the bank must give you back your original money plus the interest it earned.
Because simple interest only pays out the original amount.
Because the bank takes the interest as a fee.
Because interest subtracts from your starting money.
